requirements.requirement: Create an opsbot account on node1 and node2
requirements.summary: useradd succeeded on both nodes with locked password; id opsbot confirms uid=1001(opsbot) on node1 and node2.

requirements.requirement: Give opsbot SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2 (from node1)
requirements.summary: ed25519 keypair generated for opsbot on node1, public key installed in node2's opsbot authorized_keys, and a live SSH command (whoami/hostname) from node1's opsbot to node2's opsbot succeeded using BatchMode=yes (no password), both before and after the mandated node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on both systems
requirements.summary: A Match User opsbot block (PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey) was added and syntax-validated on both node1 and node2, sshd was reloaded, and effective config (sshd -T -C user=opsbot) confirms password auth is disabled and publickey is required on both nodes. A live password-only SSH attempt against node2's opsbot was rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)'. The behavioral password-rejection test was only performed against node2; node1's enforcement rests on the effective-config check (sshd -T -C) rather than a live rejected attempt, which is a minor evidentiary gap but not a functional gap given the authoritative nature of sshd -T -C.

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node
requirements.summary: For both node1 and node2: pre-restart boot_id/uptime/sshd/opsbot baseline was captured, a reboot was acknowledged, the node went unreachable (connection timed out) and then returned with a new boot_id (007b7197 on node1, bc8c1ee8 on node2, matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshots), and post-restart state showed sshd active, opsbot present, the publickey-only policy still enforced, authorized_keys intact on node2, and a live cross-node key-based SSH from node1's opsbot to node2's opsbot succeeding after both restarts.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material elements of the task: an opsbot account was created on both RHEL7 nodes, opsbot on node1 was given working SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2 (demonstrated live, both before and after restarts), and key-only authentication was enforced for opsbot on both nodes via a Match User block with effective-config verification and a live password-rejection test against node2. The independently required provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was executed correctly for both nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, disruption, new boot identities matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full post-restart recovery of the account, SSH policy, and cross-node key-based access. Operational hygiene is good, with only a trivial reboot-log residue and a benign retried diagnostic command.
limitations: The password-authentication-rejected behavioral test (cmd-a7c9c97a441147fc) was only performed against node2; node1's enforcement of key-only auth for opsbot is verified only via effective sshd config (sshd -T -C), not a live rejected password attempt against node1 itself.

Native package-manager consistency checks (package-health) were unavailable on both nodes in all lifecycle snapshots due to timeouts, so package-state integrity cannot be independently confirmed from this evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace shows a clean, purposeful sequence: account creation, keypair generation, key installation, sshd hardening (with syntax validation before reload), and a mandatory bounded restart cycle on each node, all directly tied to the task or the restart protocol. Two verification-only commands (cmd-7c1234363f6a42a2, cmd-652ae92aadbd43ad) partially failed because 'sshd -T -C' needs host/addr context, but the preceding 'systemctl reload sshd' in the same command still succeeded and was necessary; the failure was immediately corrected with the properly-scoped check (cmd-b93401da566a4cf3/cmd-53494613782642ee), so this is a benign diagnostic retry, not an unnecessary mutation. One read-only SSH attempt failed due to an unsupported client flag (cmd-965f6fe48ac948b3, no state change). The reboot commands left a small /tmp/reboot.log stdout-redirect file on both nodes (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff) — low-risk, expected residue from the mandated restart step rather than abandoned or unrelated state, and not indicative of a broader problem.
